# Domains Blacklist

> A DNS blocklist rebuilt daily from 45 curated upstream lists, published with
> per-source attribution, verified licences and a public cross-check of what it
> blocks among the domains people actually use.

This is a single aggregated list, not a menu of categories. Alongside
advertising, tracking, malware and phishing it also blocks gambling, piracy,
streaming and adult domains, because some upstream sources cover them. The live
breakdown is published on the statistics page. Anyone who wants only the
security categories should use a different list.

Deliberately not published here: a domain count, a source count or a file size.
Those change every night, and a number written into a document is wrong the day
after. Every figure lives in the JSON endpoints below, generated from the
artifact that was actually built.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/README.md): what the list is, what it blocks, and how to install it
- [Statistics and lookup](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/blacklists/): live figures, per-source contribution, and a search box that says whether a given domain is listed and which source supplied it
- [User guide](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/docs/USER_GUIDE.md): installation for Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, Unbound, BIND9 RPZ, Squid and uBlock Origin
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md): diagnosing a domain that is blocked or not blocked when it should be
- [Performance](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/docs/PERFORMANCE.md): sizing and configuration guidance per platform
- [Testing](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md): how to verify a deployment, and what the project's own gates check

## Downloads

- [blacklist.txt](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/releases/download/latest/blacklist.txt): one domain per line, for Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, uBlock Origin and Squid
- [unbound_blacklist.txt](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/releases/download/latest/unbound_blacklist.txt): Unbound `local-zone` directives inside a `server:` clause
- [rpz_blacklist.txt](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/releases/download/latest/rpz_blacklist.txt): a BIND9/PowerDNS response policy zone, verified loadable by `named-checkzone` before publication

## Provenance and licensing

- [SOURCES.md](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/SOURCES.md): every upstream list with its maintainer, licence and the evidence that licence was verified against
- [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/LICENSING.md): why the published list is distributed under GPL-3.0-only, how each source reaches that licence, and which questions are still open
- [NOTICES.txt](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/NOTICES.txt): the attribution that ships with each release
- [registry.json](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/sources/registry.json): the machine-readable source registry the pipeline and the site are both built from

## Data endpoints

- [stats.json](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/blacklists/data/stats.json): domain count, whitelist size, source count, and the SHA-256 of the release artifact each figure describes
- [sources.json](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/blacklists/data/sources.json): per-source HTTP status, domains contributed, and domains contributed exclusively
- [quality.json](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/blacklists/data/quality.json): which widely-used domains the list blocks, ranked, with the source responsible
- [history.json](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/blacklists/data/history.json): the daily time series
- [index.json](https://fabriziosalmi.github.io/blacklists/data/index.json): manifest for the sharded SHA-256 lookup index, which answers "is this domain listed" without downloading the whole file

## Reporting a wrongly blocked domain

- [Open a whitelist request](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/issues/new/choose): the supported route for a false positive. Check the domain on the site first - the search says which upstream source supplied it
- [Security policy](https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/blacklists/blob/main/SECURITY.md): a wrongly blocked domain is not a security issue; vulnerabilities go through a private advisory
